With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!. About the Role:. We are seeking a talented and motivated AI Engineering Intern who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement. You will join our Data Science team and play a key role in designing and building foundational A.I. systems at Sezzle. What You'll Do:. Design A.I. systems from the ground up. Generate reliable and accurate training data for our A.I. systems. Collaborate closely with engineers, data analysts, and business end users to build effective systems. Write accurate and efficient SQL queries. What We Look For:. Proficiency in SQL and Python. Solid understanding of data analysis and database structures. Currently enrolled in a postsecondary institution studying MIS, Business. Demonstrated experience working with Claude or equivalent large language model tools is required; candidates must be comfortable leveraging AI to enhance productivity, research, and communication. Analytics/Data Analytics, Computer. About You:. You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed. You're not bound by convention - your success-and much of the fun-lies in developing new ways to do things. You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking. You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly. You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle. Interview Process:. We believe transparency is important at Sezzle. Regularly providing feedback while setting expectations is part of our culture starting with the interview process. Advancement through each step is not guaranteed. Application submitted (you are here). Wonderlic test (30-40 min). SQL and Python Questions (30 minutes). Interview with recruiters (30 min). Interview with engineers (1 hour). Interview with engineering leadership (30-45 min). Offer!. Sezzle's Technology Stack:. Languages: Golang, Typescript, Python. Frontend: Typescript - React and React Native. Backend: Golang. Database: MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch. DevOps & Cloud: AWS, Kubernetes. Version Control: Git. CI/CD: Gitlab. Testing: Developer-driven, focus on automated unit, integration, and end-to-end tests. Sezzle is focused on using open source, and we build what we can before buying!. What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome:. At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators. We believe in surrounding ourselves with only the best and the brightest individuals. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire. Compensation : The salary for the A.I. Engineering Intern is $1,000 USD monthly gross. #Li-remote #Full-time.

title: AML Compliance Analyst
description: The salary range for this role is $1,800 - $2,300 per month (Gross in USD). About Sezzle. With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!. About the role:. We are seeking a detail-oriented and proactive AML Compliance Analyst to support Sezzle's Compliance Team. This role provides second-line oversight and day-to-day advisory support across a wide range of business activities by translating regulatory requirements into practical guidance, executing operational compliance reviews, and producing governance-ready documentation and reporting. This role plays a critical part in ensuring adherence to regulatory requirements and supporting the development of internal policies, standards and procedures, while fostering a culture of integrity and accountability across the organization. What You'll Do:. Provide compliance advisory support to business partners on consumer finance and payments requirements; document guidance, decisions, and follow-ups. Support the intake, tracking, and completion of Compliance Operations, Advisory, and Financial Crimes Compliance work (advisory requests, reviews, alerts/cases, and actions) using defined workflows and evidence standards. Perform second-line oversight reviews of complaint handling for higher-risk channels (e.g., CFPB, BBB, and executive escalations) and contribute to complaint trend and root-cause analysis. Support issues management governance by maintaining issue/action logs, validating remediation plans and evidence, and monitoring aging to closure. Participate in change management oversight by reviewing initiatives for compliance impacts, control readiness, and required approvals/escalations. Conduct pre-use compliance reviews of marketing and customer communications; identify required disclosures and risks (e.g., UDAAP, fair lending) and document results. Assist with product development compliance assessments for new products and material initiatives; coordinate inputs, maintain risk/control documentation, and track conditions for launch. Support third-party compliance activities for customer-facing vendors (e.g., due diligence documentation support, contract requirement tracking, ongoing monitoring). Support Financial Crimes Compliance operations, including BSA/AML transaction monitoring, alert and case review, and disposition consistent with established procedures. Assist with sanctions/OFAC screening and watchlist management, including reviewing potential matches, documenting dispositions, and escalating true or probable matches. Support Customer Identification Program (CIP) and Customer Due Diligence/Enhanced Due Diligence (CDD/EDD) activities, including identity-verification exceptions, remediation of identity defects, and program control testing. Assist in the preparation, documentation, and quality review of Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) narratives and supporting evidence, coordinating with investigators and escalating as appropriate. Advise business, product, and operations partners on financial crimes requirements and control expectations for new and existing products, and document guidance and decisions. Support responses to subpoenas and regulatory information requests, including FinCEN Section 314(a) inquiries. Prepare clear written memos and governance-ready summaries (metrics, themes, escalations) for leadership and partner reporting. Assist in gathering and delivering relevant information for internal and external regulatory reviews, examinations, audits, or other supervisory events. Support additional compliance-related initiatives and projects as assigned. Required Qualifications. Self-motivated, adaptable, and capable of working independently or collaboratively. Solid understanding of regulatory frameworks, laws, and compliance requirements applicable to consumer financial products and services, including financial crimes requirements (BSA/AML, USA PATRIOT Act, and OFAC/sanctions). Experience in compliance operations/advisory, risk management, quality assurance, or other control/oversight activities (planning, documentation, analysis, and reporting). Strong written communication skills with the ability to produce clear documentation, memos, and evidence packages. Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize effectively across multiple workstreams. Analytical thinker with sound judgment and a proactive mindset; able to recommend practical solutions that mitigate risk and strengthen controls. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage with stakeholders at all levels and provide effective challenge and recommend practical solutions to mitigate risk and enhance controls. High integrity, sound ethical judgment, and comfort escalating concerns when needed. Working knowledge of Financial Crimes Compliance operations - transaction monitoring, alert/case management, sanctions screening, CIP/CDD, and SAR processes - or a demonstrated ability to learn them quickly. Comfort working with high-volume data and structured review workflows. Self-motivated, adaptable, and capable of working independently or collaboratively in a fast-moving environment. Education & Experience. A BS/BA degree or higher in accounting, finance, business administration, legal studies, information systems, or a related field. Minimum of 3 years of professional experience in consumer finance, fintech, banking, or another regulated environment preferred. Financial industry compliance related certifications a plus (e.g. CAMS). Experience supporting complaint management oversight, issues management, change management, marketing review, product compliance assessments, financial crimes compliance (BSA/AML, sanctions, CIP/CDD, and SAR support), or third-party oversight is highly desirable. Reports To: President of Sezzle Bank and the Board Risk and Compliance Committee. About Sezzle:. With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. If you're excited about breaking new ground in tech and building products that make a real difference for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle. About Sezzle Bank (in formation):. Sezzle Bank is a planned de novo national bank in formation, headquartered in Nevada and wholly owned by Sezzle Inc. The Bank will serve as the regulated banking entity supporting Sezzle's financial product offerings and ancillary services, with a strategic focus on responsible lending, financial innovation, and exceptional customer experience. We are building a best-in-class team to stand up a safe, sound, and compliant institution from the ground up. About the Role:. We are seeking a highly experienced Chief Risk Officer to develop and maintain an effective, independent second-line risk management program for Sezzle Bank. The CRO will measure and manage credit, market, liquidity, and operational risk - with operational risk encompassing legal, compliance, and technology risk - as well as model-related risk across the Bank. Working with the Board and the Board Risk and Compliance Committee, the CRO will build the enterprise-wide risk governance framework that defines the Bank's risk culture, appetite, and limits, and will own the ongoing monitoring of these risks and of operational performance to ensure alignment with Board-approved policies and tolerances. The CRO is a Bank-only executive with no concurrent Sezzle Inc. position and reports to the President of Sezzle Bank and to the Board Risk and Compliance Committee. What You'll Do:. Risk Governance & Framework. Define enterprise-wide risk management strategies, policies, and the risk appetite framework; work with the Board and the Board Risk and Compliance Committee to establish the Bank's risk culture, appetite, and limits. Identify, assess, measure, manage, monitor, and report on risk across the Bank, and ensure compliance with Board-approved policies, tolerances, and risk limits. Identify emerging areas of risk, including potential risks associated with proposed new products and services, and ensure business strategies align with regulatory rules, guidance, and supervisory expectations. Develop and maintain a model governance framework that includes independent model validation. Participate in ALCO as the independent second-line risk perspective. Regulatory & Examination Relationship. Serve as the Bank's primary relationship manager for the OCC Examiner-in-Charge, coordinating with the Bank's President. Communicate with regulators and address regulatory inquiries and examination activities. Serve as the Bank's designated CRA Officer: administer the CRA Strategic Plan, monitor the Bank's progress against its CRA performance commitments, and ensure CRA examination readiness. Second-Line Oversight. Oversee the Bank's Chief Compliance Officer and the second-line compliance risk management function, including complaints handling and emerging regulatory and consumer compliance requirements. Oversee the Bank's BSA Officer; ensure BSA/AML/OFAC policies, procedures, risk assessments, and controls are properly designed and operationally effective. Oversee the Bank's Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) to ensure information assets, sensitive customer data, and technologies are protected; ensure the CISO reports routinely to the Board or the appropriate Board committee. Board & Business Partnership. Serve as the primary source for all risk program communication and reporting to the Board and the Board Risk and Compliance Committee. Develop and maintain strong relationships with business line management, effectively communicating emerging and present risk elements and issues. Provide support and insight to the Bank's audit program, including addressing audit findings and remediation efforts. What We Look For:. 15-20+ years of banking or financial services experience, with significant time in risk management, credit, compliance, or audit. Minimum 7-10 years in a senior risk leadership role (CRO, SVP Risk, or equivalent) at a regulated financial institution. Extensive experience managing a risk organization in a regulated banking environment, including direct experience with federal banking regulators (OCC, FDIC, or Federal Reserve) and the examination process. Deep knowledge of enterprise risk management frameworks, banking regulatory requirements, and second-line governance. Experience managing compliance, BSA/AML, OFAC, CRA, and cybersecurity risk programs. Strong communication skills with Board-level risk reporting experience. Demonstrated experience working with Claude or equivalent large language model tools is required; candidates must be comfortable leveraging AI to enhance productivity, research, and communication. Preferred Qualifications:. Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, or Mathematics; Master's degree preferred. FRM (GARP), CERP (ABA), CAMS, CRCM, or CPA certification highly valued. Experience with model risk governance and CECL/stress testing frameworks. Prior experience with de novo bank formation or building a second-line risk function from the ground up. About You:. title: Director, Litigation and Regulatory
description: About Sezzle:. With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!. About the Role:. Sezzle is a publicly traded consumer finance company (Nasdaq: SEZL) building purchase-now-pay-later products for consumers who are underserved by traditional credit, and we are pursuing a de novo national bank charter. That combination puts us in front of regulators, plaintiffs' counsel, and state enforcement authorities more often than a company our size would normally be, and we handle almost all of it in-house. This role is for a lawyer who wants to own that work rather than route it. You will run litigation and pre-litigation disputes, manage regulatory inquiries and investigations from federal and state authorities, and serve as the legal owner of our privacy and data protection framework. You will have real autonomy on day one, direct access to the executive team, and the budget discipline of a lean function that brings in outside counsel deliberately rather than reflexively. What You'll Do:. Litigation and disputes. Manage consumer litigation, class actions, arbitrations, and commercial disputes from intake through resolution, including case strategy, discovery, and settlement posture. Direct outside counsel where we use it: scope, budget, staffing, and strategy. You set the plan; they execute it. Own litigation holds, ESI protocols, custodian identification, and the discovery process end to end. Manage the small-claims and arbitration pipeline, and build the process improvements that keep volume from becoming a drag. Identify the patterns behind repeat disputes and take them back to product, operations, and collections so the underlying problem gets fixed. Regulatory inquiries and investigations. Manage civil investigative demands, examination requests, subpoenas, and informal inquiries from the CFPB, FTC, state attorneys general, and state financial regulators. Run productions: scope negotiation, data collection, privilege review, and delivery, working with engineering, data, and compliance. Draft response letters, white papers, and advocacy submissions, and participate directly in regulator meetings. Track the enforcement and supervisory landscape across BNPL, UDAAP, credit reporting, debt collection, and consumer disclosure, and translate it into concrete guidance for the business. Support supervisory readiness as we build toward bank charter approval and the examination posture that follows. Privacy and data protection. Serve as legal owner of the privacy framework: policies, notices, records of processing, data mapping, and retention. Advise on state comprehensive privacy laws, GLBA, FCRA, CAN-SPAM, TCPA, and the pixel and session-replay wiretap theories that continue to generate demand letters and class actions. Review vendor and partner data flows, negotiate data protection terms, and handle escalated consumer privacy rights requests. Partner with the Chief Compliance and Privacy Officer on incident response and on the operational privacy program. AI and how the function scales. Use AI to multiply your own throughput across research, document review, discovery, production, drafting, and regulatory tracking, and keep pushing what that stack can do. Build durable tooling, not one-off prompts: skills, workflows, templates, and automations that outlive the matter they were built for and that the rest of the team can run. Champion responsible AI adoption across the company. Legal is a builder here, not a brake. You will help business teams find ways to use these tools well and help set the guardrails that make that possible. Advise on AI governance as a legal matter: model use, vendor diligence, data handling, disclosure, and the emerging regulatory picture. Advisory and cross-functional. Counsel product, marketing, engineering, and collections on live questions with practical answers, not memos that end in "it depends.". Build the playbooks, templates, and internal training that let the function scale without adding headcount.. What We Look For:. Bachelor's degree from an accredited law school and active bar membership in good standing in at least one US jurisdiction. You will need to satisfy in-house counsel registration requirements in your home state where they apply. 5 to 7 years of combined law firm and in-house experience. Substantive consumer financial services experience. You know Reg Z, Reg B, FCRA, FDCPA, TCPA, and UDAAP as working tools, not as an outline you once memorized. Demonstrated ownership of litigation matters and regulatory inquiries, including at least some experience running them without a partner above you. Clear, direct writing. You lead with the answer. Fluent and enthusiastic use of AI as a core part of how you practice. You are not experimenting at the margins; you build workflows, prompts, and tooling that materially change your own output, and you want to keep doing that here. Demonstrated experience working with Claude or equivalent large language model tools is required; candidates must be comfortable leveraging AI to enhance productivity, research, and communication. Preferred Qualifications. BNPL, fintech, consumer lending, or bank or bank charter experience. Experience with a de novo charter application, bank supervisory examinations, or a bank partnership model. Privacy credential (CIPP/US) or substantial privacy practice. About You:. You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed. You're not bound by convention - your success-and much of the fun-lies in developing new ways to do things. You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking. You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly. You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle. We are business partners first: the job is to find the path to yes and manage the risk on the way there, not to catalogue reasons something cannot be done. We expect judgment, directness, and comfort making calls with incomplete information. We do not expect you to know everything on arrival, and we do expect you to say so when you do not. About the role:. As a Legal Intern on our Legal Operations team, you will sit exactly where paralegal work meets project management. That blend is what Legal Ops is: you will help prepare, review, and organize legal documents, and you will also keep the team's matters, deadlines, and trackers moving forward. You will work closely with our US Legal Team and with partners across Compliance, Finance, and Operations, learning first-hand how an in-house legal function runs inside a fast-growing, publicly traded fintech. We are seeking a talented and motivated Legal Intern who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement. This is a paid, fully remote internship. No prior full-time legal experience is required; curiosity, ownership, and organization matter more. What You'll Do:. Legal support (the paralegal side). Support the US Legal Team with day-to-day support requests. Review and analyze documents: review incoming liens, notices, and agreements to assess their validity, accuracy, and compliance with legal requirements, escalating anything unusual. Prepare and file documents: draft lien documents, templates, and standard forms accurately and efficiently, under the supervision of counsel or a senior paralegal, and always within deadline. Maintain the legal database: update and maintain electronic records of liens, contracts, and corporate documentation, filing and organizing everything for easy retrieval. Assist with compliance audits: support internal and external audits by pulling documentation and information related to lien processing and other legal activities. Stay informed on US legal requirements: keep up to date on relevant laws, regulations, and industry best practices, and flag anything that should change how we work. Engineer for scale and performance : build capacity models, run load and stress tests, diagnose bottlenecks across compute, networking, Kubernetes, and databases, and validate improvements against throughput, latency, saturation, and cost per workload. Build and operate the Kubernetes platform : improve cluster architecture, lifecycle automation, workload isolation, resource allocation, autoscaling, safe upgrades, and deployment reliability. Scale and optimize Aurora RDS for MySQL and Postgres : tune queries and indexes, address connection and replication bottlenecks, plan capacity, improve failover behavior, and implement safe schema changes and database migrations with application engineers. Implement and test disaster recovery : design backup, restore, and failover mechanisms against agreed recovery time and recovery point objectives; run recovery exercises and document measured results. Build infrastructure-as-code and operational automation : make provisioning, configuration, deployments, upgrades, and recovery reproducible, reviewed, testable, and recoverable. Build observability that makes production diagnosable : improve metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and actionable alerts, with visibility into service health, scaling limits, and customer impact. Improve cloud cost efficiency through technical changes : right-size resources, improve utilization, tune autoscaling and storage, and quantify savings while maintaining reliability and performance targets. Build and evaluate AI-assisted operational tooling : apply AI to investigation, runbooks, anomaly analysis, and repetitive operations, with bounded permissions, reviewable actions, and measurable improvements in accuracy or toil. Strong coding and automation skills , using Golang, Python, or similar languages to build production tooling and eliminate operational toil, alongside infrastructure-as-code experience with Terraform or equivalent. Strong systems fundamentals : Linux, networking, DNS, TLS, storage, concurrency, and distributed system failure modes, with the ability to debug problems across infrastructure and application boundaries. Experience operating a 24/7, high-availability platform where downtime has direct customer or revenue impact, including hands-on incident response and postmortem remediation. Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation and demonstrated ability to recover production systems under pressure using evidence-based triage, safe mitigation, and clear technical communication. Experience implementing and testing disaster recovery against defined recovery objectives, including restoring data and validating service recovery. Practical experience with observability, load testing, capacity planning, and safe CI/CD practices for shared production infrastructure. Active use of AI tooling in engineering or operations , with practical judgment about its limitations and how to verify generated code, recommendations, and operational actions. Ability to carry ambiguous technical problems from investigation through production delivery and collaborate across engineering disciplines to resolve system-wide constraints. Preferred Knowledge and Skills:. Experience in fintech, payments, or banking , operating infrastructure with demanding reliability, security, and audit requirements. Experience with multi-region architectures, chaos engineering, and failure testing , including the consistency and recovery tradeoffs of distributed data systems. Proficiency with Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo , or comparable observability systems. Experience building internal platform capabilities and self-service tooling , including deployment automation, progressive delivery, and reusable infrastructure components. Experience building AI-assisted incident investigation or operational automation with restricted access, auditable execution, and clear human review points. About You:. You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed. You're not bound by convention - your success-and much of the fun-lies in developing new ways to do things. You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking. You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly. You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle. You go deep : you investigate how systems behave under load and failure, follow the evidence, and fix underlying causes. You build and ship : you turn architecture into working code, tested infrastructure, and safe production changes. You measure results : you can explain the impact of your work in availability, latency, capacity, recovery time, cost, or hours of toil removed. You value simplicity : you choose systems that are understandable, operable, and appropriate to the problem, and reduce unnecessary complexity. You earn trust : you listen carefully, communicate clearly, challenge technical decisions respectfully, and follow through on commitments. You stay accountable for the outcome : you verify that changes work in production and that fixes remain effective as the platform scales. Sezzle's Technology Stack:. Languages: Golang, Python. Database: MySQL, Postgres. DevOps and Cloud: AWS, Kubernetes. Version Control: Git. CI/CD: Gitlab. Open Source: Sezzle is focused on using open source, and we build what we can before buying!. What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome?. At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators; we are skilled musicians, yogis, cyclists, chefs, golfers, dog-lovers, and rock-climbers. We believe in surrounding ourselves with not only the best and the brightest individuals, but those that are unique and purpose-driven in all that they do. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire. #Li-remote #full-time.

About the Role:. We are seeking a talented and motivated Privacy Manager who is best in class, with a high IQ plus a high EQ. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement. Sezzle is building a formal, company-wide privacy program on the NIST Privacy Framework, and we are hiring the person who will build it and run it. This is a ground-floor build with the hard parts already cleared: executive sponsorship is in place, the implementation roadmap is defined, and the core program materials are drafted. Your job is to turn that foundation into an operating program, and then to own the program as it matures. This role sits at the intersection of privacy and product. You will ensure our data practices protect our users across the US and Canada while enabling our product and engineering teams to build at speed. What You'll Do:. Build the program: Drive Sezzle's implementation of the NIST Privacy Framework from roadmap to operating program, including Current and Target Profiles, gap analysis, a prioritized and costed action plan, and ongoing monitoring, aligned with US state and federal requirements (CCPA/CPRA and other state comprehensive privacy laws, GLBA, TCPA) and Canadian privacy laws (PIPEDA and Quebec's Law 25). Run privacy review: Own privacy risk assessments and Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) for new products, features, and third-party vendors, and operate an intake and disposition process that gives every proposal a fast, documented answer: approved, approved with controls, or needs redesign. Operationalize privacy-enhancing techniques: Administer Sezzle's de-identification and aggregation standard and its approval workflow so that data-driven products and analytics ship with the right controls designed in from the start. Embed privacy-by-design: Partner directly with Engineering, Product, and Marketing teams during early-stage development so that privacy requirements are designed in, not bolted on. Govern, measure, and report: Run the cadence of Sezzle's cross-functional privacy working group, maintain the program's decision log and obligations register, track program metrics, and support executive and board-level reporting. Proven Builder: 4+ years of dedicated experience managing data privacy programs, including at least one program or major program component (a data inventory, a consumer rights operation, a privacy review process) that you stood up from early stage to steady state rather than inherited. Framework Fluency: Hands-on experience implementing a recognized privacy or security framework (NIST Privacy Framework strongly preferred; NIST CSF or ISO 27701 also relevant), including profiles or maturity assessments, gap analyses, and action plans. Deep Regulatory Knowledge: Strong working knowledge of major North American privacy frameworks (CCPA/CPRA and the broader US state privacy law landscape, TCPA, GLBA, PIPEDA, Quebec Law 25) and a sharp knack for translating complex legal mandates into clear, actionable business processes. Product-Enablement Mindset: You treat privacy as the path to yes. You are fluent in de-identification, aggregation, and other privacy-enhancing techniques as tools that let data products launch responsibly, and you can defend the line between what is de-identified and what is not. Cross-Functional Communication: High emotional intelligence (EQ) with the ability to influence technical and non-technical stakeholders alike, run a cross-functional working group, and present clearly to executives. Problem-Solving Ownership: A self-starter mindset with the ability to manage multiple high-stakes projects simultaneously in an environment where speed and agility matter. Preferred Qualifications:. CIPM (privacy program management) plus CIPP/US or CIPP/C; CIPT is a plus. Technical familiarity with modern privacy tech platforms (e.g., OneTrust, Securiti.ai, WireWheel) and data infrastructure analytics. Experience navigating financial regulations and compliance frameworks (e.g., GLBA, PCI-DSS) alongside traditional consumer privacy laws. Public-company experience, including supporting audit committee or board-level reporting. About You:. Identify and remove obstacles that could delay deal execution or partner launch. Market Intelligence & Internal Influence. Serve as Sezzle's internal subject matter expert on the government payments ecosystem. Translate partner and market feedback into product, operational, and strategic recommendations, and monitor competitive activity to bring insights back to leadership. Required. 5+ years of experience in sales, business development, payments, fintech, govtech, or a related field. Deep understanding of the government payments ecosystem, the technology platforms, payment providers, software vendors, and intermediaries that facilitate government-related payment experiences. About the Role:. We are seeking a hands-on Senior Security Engineer, Network & Zero Trust , to own the network pillar of Sezzle's zero-trust program: every connection explicitly allowed, authenticated by service identity, and attributable after the fact - across our Kubernetes clusters, AWS accounts, and the paths between them. You will take ownership of our network-policy program - default-deny micro-segmentation across our Kubernetes clusters - and carry the rest of the pillar forward with it: identity-aware service-to-service transport, per-application private access, flow-level visibility, and network configuration managed as reviewed code. This is an engineering role: you will write the policies, the tooling, and the rollout automation yourself, and you will carry changes through other teams' services without breaking delivery. You will report to the Director of Information Security and work alongside the engineers who own the security platform and detection and response, and with the platform and IAM teams on service identity - your network controls are what their work relies on, and your telemetry is what their detections run on. At Sezzle, AI-assisted engineering is a standard part of how we work. In this role you will use and build agentic workflows - flow analysis, policy generation from observed traffic, drift review - that let the team segment a large estate. What You'll Do:. Own east-west segmentation across our Kubernetes clusters: design the segmentation model, derive network policies from observed traffic, and keep every workload reachable only through explicitly allowed, identity-bound paths - a default that holds as the estate grows, not a one-time project. Deliver identity-aware transport - design and roll out mutually authenticated, encrypted service-to-service connections (mTLS), so that authorization decisions rest on verified service identity. Keep a live map of the network: VPC peerings, tunnels, cross-account links, and every public entry point - built from cloud APIs and reconciled continuously, so every path into production is known and justified. Own segmentation of production and the cardholder-data environment: implement and enforce the CDE and high-trust-tier boundaries, review every peering and public exposure against them, and run segmentation testing with the security team. Partner with IT on private access: evaluate and help deliver per-application access (ZTNA) for engineers and operators reaching production systems. Own network telemetry: flow logs east-west and north-south, with enough identity on both ends that "who talked to what, when" is answerable in minutes - and feed it to our SIEM for the detection team. Own cluster admission control and hold the line on drift: workload admission policy (pod security, image provenance, network policy), security groups and firewall rules declared in git, applied only through the IaC pipeline, with admission control at the gate and drift detected and reverted automatically. Contain: build the levers that let us isolate a workload or segment quickly when detection flags lateral movement, and take part in incident response when the network is in play. Participate in threat modeling and design reviews for anything that changes how traffic flows, and in the on-call rotation for the controls you own. What We Look For:. 6+ years of experience in security, network, platform, or infrastructure engineering, with hands-on ownership of network controls in cloud production environments. . Deep, practical Kubernetes networking knowledge: CNI, NetworkPolicy semantics, DNS, ingress/egress - and experience rolling segmentation out on live clusters without outages. . Strong AWS networking: VPCs, subnets, security groups, peering and Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, load balancers, flow logs.. Hands-on experience with mTLS and service-to-service authentication (service mesh, proxies, or CNI-level encryption). Infrastructure as code as your default way of working - Terraform and Helm or equivalents, through merge requests and CI, across repositories you don't own. Ability to write real code (Go, Python, or Bash) for tooling and automation, not only configuration. Ability to investigate directly with packet captures, flow logs, and system-level data. Working knowledge of PCI DSS network requirements - segmentation, scoping of the cardholder-data environment, segmentation testing. Demonstrated AI-forward engineering: you actively use AI tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or custom LLM integrations) in your work today and have opinions grounded in practice about where it helps and where it doesn't. Preferred Knowledge and Skills:. Cilium / eBPF in production, including Hubble or equivalent flow observability. mTLS at fleet scale, including certificate lifecycle - service mesh (e.g., Istio, Linkerd, Cilium service mesh) and workload identity standards such as SPIFFE/SPIRE. You have built AI-assisted workflows that others adopted - flow analysis, policy generation, drift review. Experience evaluating or deploying ZTNA / identity-aware proxy products. ● Policy-as-code and admission control (OPA/Gatekeeper, Kyverno, conftest). Experience with network detection - IDS/IPS, anomalous-flow and lateral-movement detection - and with containment during incidents. Familiarity with SOC 2 and with FFIEC-style examination expectations for network security. ● Experience in fintech, payments, BNPL, or other regulated environments. About You:. We are seeking a hands-on Senior Software Engineer, Security Platform, to build and own the platform the security team runs on: the services that discover, scan, triage and route security findings, the event-driven bus that connects them, and the CI security gates every team's pipeline runs through. This is a development role on the security team, not a security-analyst role. Most of your time goes into designing, building and operating services in Go and Python on Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, the existing fleet where it has grown faster than its upkeep, and the NATS-based event platform that moves findings, inventory changes and notifications between them. The security gates in our GitLab CI (SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning) and the agentic triage and review workflows are part of that platform, not the whole of it. Your job is to make these systems fast, low-noise, and reliable enough to be trusted by default without slowing delivery. You will report to the Director of Information Security and work alongside the engineers who own detection and response and network and zero trust - your platform is what their work composes with. At Sezzle, AI-assisted engineering is a standard part of how we build. In this role you will build reusable agentic workflows (Claude Code skills, CI review agents, automated triage and verification) that multiply what the team can cover, and hold that review discipline in the platform code you own. What You'll Do:. Design, build, and operate security engineering services primarily in Golang and Python, on AWS and Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, and the upkeep, hardening and retirement of the existing ones. Own the event-driven platform between the security services: the NATS bus, its contracts and consumers, delivery guarantees and observability - so a finding, an inventory change or an alert reaches every service that acts on it. Integrate the platform end-to-end: scanners → finding system-of-record → tickets → metrics, so remediation state is visible and exam evidence is a by-product of engineering. Own delivery of the security gates - SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning: scanner selection and tuning, suppression workflow mechanics, false-positive burn-down, and the rollout tooling that takes a gate from advisory reporting to enforcing without blocking delivery. Build agentic security workflows: CI review agents, automated finding triage and verification, remediation helpers - tooling other engineers actually adopt. Build the triage-to-remediation automation: validate true positives by hand enough to prove the tooling right, then automate the loop - reproduction context, fix guidance, and routing to the owning teams and to vulnerability-management operations. Participate in threat modeling and secure design reviews for the services you build and the pipelines you own. Participate in the on-call rotation for the services you own. What We Look For:. 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant backend experience. . Deployed significant changes to a production application in the past 30 days. . Strong proficiency in Golang, plus working proficiency in Python. . Hands-on experience building and operating event-driven or message-based systems (NATS, Kafka, or similar): contracts, idempotent consumers, replay, back-pressure. . Hands-on experience building and operating CI/CD pipeline tooling - jobs, shared templates, runners - GitLab CI at fleet scale is a strong plus. . Hands-on web application security knowledge: the OWASP Top 10 in real code - able to find these issues, fix them yourself, and encode the detection so they stop recurring. . Working knowledge of AWS and Kubernetes as deployment targets for the services you build. Preferred Knowledge and Skills:. Experience in fintech, payments, BNPL, or consumer lending, especially with systems in cardholder-data or regulated scope. Working knowledge of PCI DSS and SOC 2 as they apply to software development and change management - the platform you build is what produces that evidence. Software supply-chain integrity: SBOM pipelines, dependency governance, artifact signing and provenance (Sigstore, SLSA). Familiarity with policy-as-code and admission control (OPA, Kyverno, conftest) - your gates compose with the cluster's runtime policy-enforcement layer. Exposure to bug bounty or external vulnerability report triage - enough to know what the automation you build has to get right. Experience with threat modeling at a system level. About You:. You measure yourself by other teams' code - a fix you shipped is good; a vulnerability class that stopped appearing across the fleet is better. You'd rather ship a gate than publish a policy - you know that enforcement changes behavior and documents do not, and you build the enforcement so well that engineers want to keep it. You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed. You're not bound by convention - your success-and much of the fun-lies in developing new ways to do things. You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking. You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.. . You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.. DevOps & Cloud: AWS, Kubernetes. Version Control: Git. CI/CD: Gitlab. Testing: Developer and AI-driven, focus on automated end-to-end, integration, and unit tests. Sezzle is building the platform that will carry us from a BNPL provider into a full-stack financial institution. This role owns the system at the center of that: Sezzle's banking core - the ledger, accounts and balances, and the money movement that every future Sezzle financial product will run on. You would own it end to end. Discovery, architecture and vendor decisions, requirements, build, launch, and everything after - not a slice of someone else's roadmap, but the full product lifecycle for the platform itself. You'd work directly with Engineering, Finance, Compliance, Treasury, and Risk, with real authority over how this gets built. Ideally you've built something like this before. If you haven't, but you've owned a ledger, a payments platform, an issuing program, or other financial infrastructure - and you're the kind of person who learns a domain properly rather than around the edges - we want to talk to you. What matters most is that you've owned real infrastructure and that you're willing to go deep on the parts you don't know yet. What You'll Do:. Own the banking platform roadmap. Define and sequence the platform work required to support accounts, deposits, cards, and lending on a single ledger and account model. Help drive the build-vs-buy decision. Evaluate core banking platforms and processors, run vendor diligence, model cost and time-to-market, and help leadership decide whether we extend what we have or integrate a third party. Shape the account and ledger model. Work with Engineering and Finance on account hierarchies, sub-ledgers, chart-of-accounts mapping, posting rules, holds, interest and fee accrual, and general ledger integration. Specify money movement. Own product requirements for transfers, ACH, card issuing and network settlement, real-time rails, and returns and reversals - including exception handling, cutoff windows, and settlement reconciliation. Make the platform auditable. Ensure the system produces the reporting, traceability, and controls that Finance, audit, and regulators need - reconciliation breaks, balance attestation, and complete transaction history. Partner on regulatory readiness. Work with Compliance and Legal to turn their requirements into platform capabilities: screening hooks, onboarding data, error resolution, disclosures and statements, and reporting. You don't need to arrive fluent in US banking regulation - you do need to be someone who learns it properly. Plan migration and cutover. If a migration is in scope, own data mapping, parallel-run strategy, validation criteria, rollback plans, and phased cutover. Write the technical requirements. Own detailed specs, API contracts, event schemas, data models, user stories, and release plans end-to-end. Use data to prove it works. Write your own SQL. Define platform KPIs - posting latency, reconciliation break rate, settlement accuracy, failure rates - and monitor them relentlessly. Manage risk early. Anticipate technical risks, edge cases, race conditions, and dependencies before they become incidents. Money movement defects are the expensive kind. Operate with urgency. Bachelor's or advanced degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or other technical discipline (required). 5-10 years of product experience, with meaningful time spent on financial infrastructure rather than only customer-facing surfaces. Ledgers, general ledger, or balance and transaction systems. Payments processing, orchestration, or money movement - ACH, card networks, transfers, settlement, or the LATAM equivalents (PIX, SPEI, PSE, CCE). Card issuing or card program management. Deposit, wallet, or account platforms. Lending origination or loan servicing platforms. Product work at a processor, BaaS provider, or core banking vendor. Comfort with double-entry accounting concepts as they show up in software - debits and credits, sub-ledgers, accruals, reconciliation - or a genuine appetite to get comfortable with them quickly. Deep technical understanding of APIs, event-driven architecture, idempotency, distributed system failure modes, batch vs. real-time processing, and data flows. Strong SQL skills and comfort querying and interpreting data independently. Experience working directly with Compliance, Legal, Finance, or Treasury as stakeholders - not only Engineering and Design. Comfortable working in ambiguity and making sound, documented decisions with incomplete information. Strong written and verbal communication - can hold your own in an engineering standup, a Finance review, and an executive discussion. title: Solutions Engineer
description: Job Title: Solutions Engineer. About Sezzle:. With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!. About the Role:. We are seeking a talented and motivated Solutions Engineer who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement. As a Solutions Engineer, you are the technical owner of the merchant relationship from first sales conversation through live integration and beyond. You will focus on our enterprise and strategic merchants: the national retailers and high-volume brands running custom, hand-built integrations across web, mobile app, and in-store. These are our most complex merchants and our largest revenue drivers, and they do not come with an off-the-shelf plugin. You will partner with Sales, Product, and Engineering to scope what a merchant needs, design the integration that gets them there, and stay with them once they are live. You own the technical side of pre-sales: demos, architecture discussions, RFP responses, and solution proposals. When a merchant needs something custom, you define the requirement, shape the solution with our engineering team, and drive it to launch. This is a customer-facing engineering role. You will spend as much time on calls with merchant developers as you will in documentation and test environments, and you need to be credible in both rooms. This role combines technical expertise and sales acumen to support sales teams. They work closely with the sales team and clients, understanding customer needs and translating them into effective, tailored solutions. Acting as a bridge between technical and business functions, a Solutions Engineer not only helps demonstrate and implement the product's capabilities but also communicates complex technical details in a way that resonates with clients. Their role requires both the ability to engage with customers directly and the technical know-how to ensure the product meets client requirements effectively. What You'll Do:. Own technical discovery for prospective merchants: understand their stack, their checkout flow, and their constraints, then map them to the right Sezzle integration path. Lead product demos and technical presentations for merchant engineering and business stakeholders. Design integration solutions across our API, SDKs, and platform plugins (Shopify, BigCommerce, Magento, WooCommerce, Wix, and custom builds). Write technical proposals and complete RFP and security questionnaire responses. Support merchant mobile app integrations: SDK implementation, in-app checkout, and native versus webview handoff. Validate integrations in sandbox and in production before launch, including checkout flow, widget and messaging placement, redirect and handoff behavior, and settlement. Troubleshoot live integration issues alongside Support and Engineering, and own the technical narrative back to the merchant. Translate recurring merchant needs into product feedback, and push for the fixes that unblock revenue. Build and maintain integration documentation, runbooks, and internal enablement so the team scales without you in every call. Act as the trusted technical advisor for your merchants after launch, spotting optimization opportunities they haven't asked for yet. What We Look For:. 4+ years in a customer-facing technical role: solutions engineering, sales engineering, implementation, solutions architecture, or technical account management. Experience with mobile SDK integrations on iOS and Android, including the ability to guide merchant mobile developers through implementation and debug what breaks. Experience supporting enterprise merchants through complex, multi-stakeholder integrations with custom-built commerce stacks. Hands-on experience with REST APIs, webhooks, and reading API documentation critically. Working knowledge of web technologies: HTML, CSS, JavaScript. Familiarity with at least one major e-commerce platform (Shopify, BigCommerce, Magento, WooCommerce, Wix) and how payment methods integrate into it. Understanding of e-commerce workflows: cart, checkout, payment authorization and capture, refunds, shipping, and product management. Ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, and business context clearly to engineers. Strong written communication. You will produce documentation and proposals that merchants and internal teams rely on. Comfort managing several merchant integrations at once in a fast-moving environment. Ability to read code in at least one language well enough to debug a merchant's implementation. Demonstrated ability to use AI tools effectively in day-to-day work, including research, technical documentation, problem-solving, and workflow automation. Preferred Qualifications. title: Supplier Performance and Relationship Management Specialist
description: Supplier Performance and Relationship Management Specialist The Opportunity:. In this role, you'll support Booz Allen's enterprise Supplier Performance Management (SPM) and Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) frameworks by executing structured supplier performance evaluations, coordinating governance activities, strengthening supplier relationships, and improving visibility into supplier health, risk, and delivery outcomes. You'll work closely with procurement managers, program managers (PMs), category teams, and other stakeholders to ensure supplier accountability and continuous improvement across the supply base.. We need a specialist like you to support SPM operational cycles by identifying supplier populations aligned to segmentation criteria and contract lifecycle triggers. You'll deploy supplier scorecards in Ivalua and upon completion, you'll analyze performance results which will be reported in monthly roll‑ups and leadership reviews. Based on identified performance trends and risks, you'll collaborate with internal stakeholders to draft, distribute, and track Letters of Concern (LOCs) and Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) as part of the supplier remediation process. Your work will promote transparency, defensibility, and traceability throughout supplier performance monitoring and follow-up actions.. You'll also support the management of strategic and business-critical supplier relationships. You'll use supplier performance data and stakeholder insights to coordinate and facilitate governance activities, including quarterly business reviews, performance discussions, and risk escalations. Your efforts contribute to an integrated supplier management operating model, linking SPM, SRM, segmentation, and risk management to strengthen supplier accountability, enable strategic supplier engagement, improve reliability, and support long‑term value creation for Booz Allen. Due to the nature of work performed within this facility, U.S. citizenship is required.. What You'll Work On:. Support day‑to‑day relationship management activities for strategic and business-critical suppliers, helping maintain structured governance and performance oversight. Coordinate governance cadences, including monthly operational reviews, Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), and annual strategic business reviews. Prepare governance meeting materials, track action items, document supplier performance outcomes, and escalate risks to procurement managers or SRM leads as needed. Monitor KPIs, SLAs, and relationship management indicators to assess supplier collaboration, responsiveness, and strategic alignment. Support supplier segmentation updates by gathering data on spend, risk, criticality, and performance trends. Contribute to maintaining governance cadence discipline and ensuring supplier engagement aligns with segmentation guidance. Identify supplier populations for recurring scorecard cycles using segmentation criteria. Deploy supplier scorecards in Ivalua and ensure PMs and buyers receive correct evaluations. Follow up with PMs and buyers on incomplete or overdue scorecards. Reassign evaluations when routing issues or responsibility changes occur. Troubleshoot scorecard routing, assignment, and reviewer workflow issues across PM or GSC stakeholders. Track supplier performance results across scorecard cycles, monitoring trends and identifying emerging quality, delivery, cost, or communication issues. Support reporting by compiling supplier performance metrics, completion data, risk indicators, and scorecard insights for dashboards and leadership reviews. Highlight supplier performance issues requiring remediation, and support the development of LOCs or CAPs. Maintain structured, defensible documentation of supplier performance activities, including evidence used for evaluations, escalations, and governance.. Join us. The world can't wait.. You Have:. 2+ years of experience in supplier-facing roles such as supply chain, procurement, vendor management, subcontract management, or logistics. Experience conducting performance assessments, supplier reviews, quality or compliance checks, or vendor scorecard evaluations. Experience supporting issue resolution, corrective action management, or escalation processes. title: Software Development Technical Planner
description: Software Development Technical Planner The Opportunity:. We are seeking an experienced, detail-oriented Software Development Technical Planner to orchestrate and streamline our software delivery lifecycle. In this critical role, you will bridge the gap between engineering execution, program management, and technical delivery. You will be primarily responsible for formulating, maintaining, and managing comprehensive software build plans, end-to-end integrated master schedules (IMS), and release tracks. Working directly with software architects, development leads, QA, and configuration management, you will anticipate dependencies, mitigate delivery bottlenecks, and ensure complex software deliverables ship reliably and on time.. Architect, baseline, and maintain comprehensive software build plans and integration schedules across multiple product teams and release trains. Define and sequence critical path activities from code commit, static analysis, and automated test passes through staging, security audits, and production deployment. Coordinate build cadence, branching strategies, and merge schedules in close collaboration with DevOps and Configuration Management teams. Align build milestones with target hardware integration, third-party software drops, and customer integration schedules. Build and manage Integrated Master Schedules (IMS) utilizing industry-standard scheduling and project management methodologies. Track schedule progress against performance baselines. Analyze critical paths, variance, floats, and schedule health metrics. Facilitate regular technical syncs, scrum-of-scrums, and build review forums to ensure operational alignment across disparate development modules. Synthesize raw engineering progress into clear, data-driven executive dashboards and schedule health status reports. Identify, map, and proactively track complex technical cross-team dependencies, technical debt bottlenecks, and deliverables. Conduct regular technical risk and opportunity assessments. Formulate proactive mitigation playbooks to prevent schedule slippage. Lead schedule impact assessments and root cause analyses when change requests, scope adjustments, or critical blocking bugs arise. Collaborate with Product Managers, Technical Leads, Systems Engineers, and QA Leads to translate system requirements into granular engineering work breakdown structures (WBS). Drive continuous improvement by establishing post-release retrospectives, refining scheduling models, and optimizing technical planning workflows.. Join us. The world can't wait. . You Have:. 4+ years of experience in technical program management, software project management, or technical planning within a software engineering environment. Experience developing and managing structured software build plans and integrated schedules for complex, multi-team software initiatives. Experience in project scheduling tools and enterprise scheduling software such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or Primavera P6. Experience with modern software development and issue-tracking platforms such as Jira, Jira Align, Azure DevOps, or Confluence. Experience with both Agile frameworks such as Scrum, Kanban, or SAFe and traditional Waterfall or Milestone-driven methodologies. Knowledge of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), CI/CD pipelines, build systems, branching and merging strategies such as Gitflow or trunk-based development, and QA test automation phases. Ability to present complex schedule data clearly to both developers and senior leadership. Ability to obtain a Secret clearance. Bachelor's degree in technical discipline such as Computer Science, Software Engineering, Systems Engineering, or Information Systems. Nice If You Have:. Experience working in complex environments such as embedded systems, aerospace and defense, automotive, telecom, or distributed cloud platforms where hardware and software co-dependencies exist. Experience with software safety and compliance standards such as ISO 26262, DO-178C, IEC 62304, SOC 2, or ISO 27001, where rigorous planning and auditing are paramount. Ability to build automation and release orchestrators such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or ArgoCD. Ability to construct automated reporting dashboards using tools like Tableau, Power BI, Jira Advanced Roadmaps, or custom Python or SQL reporting scripts. PMP Certification, PMI-SP Certification, Certified ScrumMaster Certification, or Agile Certified Practitioner Certification. Clearance:. title: Cloud Security Engineer
description: Cloud Security Engineer The Opportunity:. Everyone is trying to "harness the cloud," but not everyone knows how to secure it. As a security engineer, you know how to assess and implement requirements that ensure the safety of information systems and protect them against intentional or inadvertent access or destruction. What if you could use your cloud security skills to improve mission critical applications for the Intelligence Community (IC)? We need you to help us develop cloud-based security architectures for some of the IC's most critical systems.. As a security engineer on our team, you'll evaluate and support the documentation, validation, assessment, and accreditation processes necessary to ensure that Information Technology (IT) systems meet the organization's Information Assurance (IA) and security requirements. You'll assist in defining organizations' desired state and risk thresholds and analyze actual state information to assess compliance. You'll work with leaders to advise on codifying strategic objectives into doctrine and procedures that can help meet defined objectives. You'll assist with evaluation of computer applications, software, or specialized utility programs to determine if software assurance best practices are followed. You'll recommend tools and capabilities based on your research of the current environment and knowledge of various on-premise, cloud-based, and hybrid resources to address security requirements. You will implement the cloud security architectures, tools, and processes that you helped to shape and define. Your technical experience will be vital as you work with IC clients to ensure standards are met with security requirements. This is an opportunity to use the latest cloud technologies as you look for ways to secure your customer's environment while collaborating with tomorrow's cloud security experts. This position is located in Reston, Virginia.. Join us. The world can't wait.. Experience with security architecture evaluations, guidance development, and troubleshooting. Experience with the Risk Management Framework (RMF). Active TS/SCI clearance; willingness to take a polygraph exam. HS diploma or GED. Ability to obtain a DoD 8570 IAT Level III Certification such as SecurityX, CCNP Security, CISA, CISSP, GCED, GCIH, or CCSP Certification within 30 days of start date. Ability to obtain a DoD 8570 Cybersecurity Service Provider-Infrastructure Support Certification (CSSP-IS), including CEH, CySA+, GICSP, SSCP, CHFI, CFR, Cloud+, or CND Certification within 30 days of start date. . title: AI and ML Data Scientist
description: AI and ML Data Scientist The Opportunity:. As an Agentic AI Engineer and Data Scientist for military intelligence, you're excited by the opportunity to design, develop, and deploy advanced AI systems that help analysts transform complex, fragmented information into actionable intelligence. You understand the possibilities created by large language models (LLMs), machine learning (ML), natural language processing (NLP), autonomous workflows, and multi-agent architectures, and you want to apply them to mission-critical national security challenges.. In today's contested and information-rich operating environment, military intelligence teams must rapidly make sense of large volumes of structured and unstructured data from multiple sources, formats, and domains. As an AI professional at Booz Allen, you'll help build intelligent systems that support intelligence discovery, analysis, prioritization, reporting, and decision advantage for defense and national security clients.. On our team, you'll use your AI, data science, and software development skills to create real-world mission impact. You'll work closely with clients, analysts, engineers, and mission stakeholders to understand operational needs, identify high-value use cases, and develop agentic AI capabilities that can reason over data, orchestrate workflows, retrieve relevant information, generate analytic products, and support human-in-the-loop decision-making. You'll design and implement AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, evaluation frameworks, prompt strategies, data processing workflows, and mission-focused prototypes. You'll help ensure these systems are reliable, explainable, secure, testable, and aligned to operational requirements. Ultimately, you'll help military intelligence organizations use AI responsibly and effectively to accelerate insight, improve analytic tradecraft, and support informed decisions.. Work with us as we develop advanced AI capabilities for the mission. . Join us. The world can't wait. . Experience developing, integrating, or evaluating AI, ML, NLP, LLMs, or agentic AI capabilities for mission, operational, or enterprise use cases, and building AI-enabled applications using Python and modern AI/ML libraries or frameworks, including PyTorch, Scikit-Learn, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Hugging Face, or CUDA. Experience developing agentic AI systems, including autonomous or semi-autonomous agents, tool-using agents, multi-step reasoning workflows, task orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, or human-in-the-loop AI capabilities. Experience designing, testing, validating, or evaluating AI/ML systems, including model performance, accuracy, relevance, robustness, hallucination mitigation, or mission-aligned evaluation criteria and analyzing, processing, and integrating structured and unstructured data sources, including intelligence data such as text, reports, messages, metadata, documents, or geospatial data. description: Cloud Network Engineer The Opportunity:. We are seeking a Senior Network Engineer to support the design, deployment, and maintenance of enterprise and tactical networks for the Department of War (DoW). This is an exciting opportunity to apply your expertise in wireless networking, , and cybersecurity to build secure and resilient infrastructure that directly impacts mission readiness and quality-of-life for military personnel and their families. title: Healthcare Integration Engineer, Senior
description: Healthcare Integration Engineer, Senior The Opportunity:. Are you looking for an opportunity to create technical synergy that will modernize and secure the flow of clinical and laboratory data across the federal health enterprise? As an integration engineer, you know the importance of ensuring clinical applications, laboratory systems, and messaging interfaces work together. You're eager to apply your health IT and interoperability knowledge to develop creative solutions.. On our team, you'll design, develop, and implement solutions for software integration projects across functions or between organizations that'll directly impact patient care and public health reporting. Using HL7v2 and FHIR standards, interface lifecycle processes, and an Agile framework, you'll work alongside software development engineers to integrate laboratory information management systems, EHRs, and cloud-hosted clinical applications. You'll use tools like Rhapsody, Azure, GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and modern observability stacks to plan, organize, and conduct integration projects that meet design specifications and standards from inception to completion.. In this role, you'll impact the health mission by guaranteeing that lab results, orders, and clinical documents move reliably and securely between systems that were never designed to talk to each other and by building the monitoring and alerting that proves it. With opportunities to learn new tools and skills, we focus on growing and collaborating as a team to make the best solutions for our customers. This role is located in Atlanta, GA. . Work with us as we integrate new solutions for the federal health mission.. Join us. The world can't wait.. You Have:. 5+ years of experience in software or systems integration. Experience developing, testing, and deploying HL7 interfaces in an integration engine such as Rhapsody, Mirth Connect, Corepoint, or InterSystems. Experience with HL7v2 message structures, including ADT, ORM, ORU, and SIU message types. Experience with infrastructure automation and scripting in Python, PowerShell, or Bash and CI/CD pipeline development using GitHub Actions, including workflow authoring, reusable workflows, and secrets management. Experience deploying and supporting applications in a cloud environment. Knowledge of interface troubleshooting across the full path, including TCP, MLLP, SFTP, and REST transport layers. Knowledge of observability practices, including logging, metrics, distributed tracing, alerting, and SLO definition. Ability to diagnose production interface failures and drive root cause analysis under time pressure. Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust or Suitability/Fitness determination based on client requirements. Bachelor's degree. . Nice If You Have:.
